x: Warm sea water, above about 26–27°C, supplies the heat and moisture that power a tropical cyclone. The other conditions help organise it.
t: Discriminate the energy source from other conditions.

x: Option C is incorrect: the centre of a cyclone has the lowest pressure, not the highest. The calm eye, violent eyewall and spiral rainbands are right.
t: Check for a reversed pressure.

x: Both are true and R explains A: within about 5° of the Equator the Coriolis force is too weak to set the air spinning.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: A is true: temperate cyclones form where contrasting air masses meet. B is false because the westerlies carry them from west to east.
t: Check each statement for a reversed direction.

x: I, II and III are correct: anticyclones have a high-pressure centre with sinking air flowing outward. IV is false because they bring calm, clear weather.
t: Discriminate cyclone from anticyclone weather.

x: Cumulus shows convective growth, cumulonimbus brings thunderstorms and hail, nimbostratus gives prolonged rain and cirrostratus is a high cloud, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Recall the weather of each cloud type.

x: Hurricanes strike the USA and Atlantic, typhoons China and the western Pacific, willy-willies north-west Australia, and Nargis hit Myanmar, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
t: Recall the regional names of cyclones.

x: Option C is incorrect: Western Disturbance rainfall decreases from west to east across the north-western plains. They are Mediterranean-born extratropical systems of winter.
t: Check for a reversed direction.

x: All four are local disturbances: thunderstorms, tornadoes, cloudbursts and local squalls.
t: Discriminate local from large-scale disturbances.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: high pressure with outflow does not by itself give the direction; the Coriolis force makes it clockwise in the north.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: A tropical cyclone is a low over warm seas, a temperate cyclone comes from air-mass interaction, an anticyclone is a high with outflow and a thunderstorm is a local convective storm, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall the definition of each disturbance.

x: Both are true: a thunderstorm is a violent convective storm with lightning, and a tornado is a violently rotating funnel.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Both are true: Western Disturbances are regional systems steered by the westerlies and the subtropical westerly jet.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: All four are correct: instability, low wind shear and an existing disturbance are needed to start and organise a tropical cyclone.
t: Recall the conditions for cyclone formation.

x: The key picks D: the eye is a calm, fair, warmer centre. It is also the lowest-pressure part of the cyclone, so C is true as well. Rainbands and the eyewall are the other choices.
t: Discriminate eye, eyewall and rainbands.

x: All five are correct: cyclones turn anticlockwise in the north and clockwise in the south, and anticyclones do the reverse.
t: Recall the rotation in each hemisphere.

x: All three are correct: in India the storm is simply called a cyclone, and its air flows inward and rises.
t: Recall the air flow of a cyclone.

x: Both are true: temperate cyclones occur at about 35°–65° in both hemispheres and form along fronts.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Both are true: Western Disturbances bring snow to the mountains and winter rain that matters for rabi crops.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Gulf of Mexico air supplies warm moisture to tornado-prone USA, cold dry air and instability contribute to tornadoes and wind shear produces supercells. The code pairs items in order when List-II repeats, giving a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.
t: Recall the ingredients of tornadoes.

x: Both are true and R explains A: tornadoes spin out of severe rotating convection, which supercells provide.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: All three are correct: anticyclones and thunderstorms occur in many regions, and tornadoes in severe-storm regions.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: None of the four has fronts: tropical cyclones, anticyclones, thunderstorms and tornadoes. Fronts belong to temperate cyclones.
t: Recall which systems have fronts.

x: Tropical cyclones have cumulonimbus and rainbands, temperate cyclones stratiform and cumuliform cloud, thunderstorms cumulonimbus and tornadoes cumulonimbus supercells, giving a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Recall the clouds of each disturbance.
